text:
mike: Heads-up — just saw a bad interaction between the Terraform nodegroup update and the GitOps deployer during the eu-west-3 rollout. GPU pods stuck Pending because taints/labels didn't match after autoscaler renamed the pool.
sara: Ugh. Do you have the apply log? which change triggered it?
mike: Terraform changed `node_pool_name` (we renamed for billing tags), autoscaler detected new ASG and applied taints via userdata race. Root message TS 1882467000.
jordan: Can you paste the kube events for one of the pods?
mike: Sure, here's one of the events: ```
Normal SchedulingAttempt  5s  default-scheduler  No nodes are available that match taints: application=gpu:NoSchedule.
Warning FailedScheduling  3s  default-scheduler  0/12 nodes are available: 12 node(s) had taint {application=gpu:NoSchedule}, that the pod didn't tolerate.
```
sara: So Terraform rename -> ASG recreation -> nodes come up with taint but our deployment expects `gpu=true` label + toleration `application/gpu`. Mismatch between label vs taint semantics.
lee: That's the kubelet/userdata bootstrap step: we apply label `node.kubernetes.io/gpu=true` but autoscaler hooks apply taint `application=gpu`. Two different conventions in two places.
mike: Right. GitOps flux applied the node pool helm chart at the same time as the terraform change. They raced: terraform created instances, flux rendered the chart to set daemonset that applies labels, but autoscaler hook ran after bootstrap and reapplied taint.
sara: How widespread? just eu-west-3 canary cluster or prod?
mike: Canary cluster only so far, but the same job is queued for prod tomorrow.
jordan: We should abort the prod rollout. Also add a preflight gate in the GitOps pipeline: check label/taint policy before promoting.
lee: Agreed. Quick mitigation: add toleration to workloads to accept `application/gpu:NoSchedule` until we consolidate naming. Then run a reconciliation job to align labels -> taints mapping.
devops-bot: Scheduled run: `infra/preflight-check` for prod nodepool rename at 1882467150. See CI link: https://ci.redwood/infra/preflight/1882467150
sara: For longer-term: standardize on one source of truth — either the autoscaler hook sets labels or our bootstrap sets taints. My vote: keep kube labels via userdata, and have autoscaler drop taints.
jordan: Also we need to avoid ASG replacement on name-only changes. Can we change TF to do in-place rename (tag update) instead of resource replacement?
mike: I dug into the plan: provider forces replacement if `name` field changes. We can instead manage billing tags via `tags` map and leave name stable.
lee: Pipeline changes: add `preflight-terraform-plan` job that runs a `kubectl get nodes,taints -o json` and compares expected taint/label mapping. Fail pipeline if mismatch. Pseudocode: ```bash
EXPECTED_TAINTS='application=gpu:NoSchedule'
NODE_TAINTS=$(kubectl get nodes -l app=gpu -o jsonpath='{.items[*].spec.taints[*].key}:{.items[*].spec.taints[*].effect}')
if [[ "$NODE_TAINTS" != "$EXPECTED_TAINTS" ]]; then exit 1; fi
```
sara: And add a small canary step: provision 2 nodes, wait for node-labels to converge, then continue. Also a 10-minute hold after create to let bootstrap/daemonsets finish.
jordan: We should also add a terraform `prevent_destroy` lifecycle for the GPU nodepool resource to avoid accidental replace on small changes.
mike: For immediate prod stop, I cancelled the prod pipeline at 1882467185. Please don't re-run until we merge fixes.
lee: I'll open a PR to update Helm chart to apply labels (not taints) and add toleration patch into workload overlays as temporary.
sara: I'll update the GitOps job to run the preflight script and a `tf plan` parser to detect replacements.
devops-bot: Incident note created: INFRA-2026-045 - nodepool naming -> taint/label mismatch on canary. Link: https://tickets.redwood/INFRA-2026-045
mike: TL;DR: stop rename-in-place via TF, add pipeline preflight, add short toleration fallback, run a reconciliation to unify conventions before prod. :thumbsup:
